sessions.blurb: Rejoice! Thou art now a subject of the Crown Kingdom.

lines.text: Rejoice! Thou art now a subject of the Crown Kingdom.
Hmm? Didst thou think any mere knave could earn such honor?

choices.text: Huh? I thought anyone could become one.
Thanks, it's an honor.

lines.text: How could it be so?
Only after one hath received the grace of Her Highness and myself
shalt they be granted the right to become a subject of the Crown Kingdom.
Aye, that is the attitude of a true subject.
Live always in gratitude for the boundless grace of Her Highness!
Chime and I talk about the subjects of the Crown Kingdom.

sessions.blurb: Truly, the more I behold Her Highness, the more splendid she seemeth.

lines.text: Truly, the more I behold Her Highness, the more splendid she seemeth.

choices.text: You mean the way she protects you?
You mean the way she craves food?

lines.text: Aye, 'tis exactly so!
When Her Highness doth stand afore me, shielding me...
Knowest thou how magnificently she doth shine, how steadfastly my heart is eased?
Nay, "magnificently" doth scarce suffice!
She is naught but the light itself!
R-Rapscallion!
How dare thou speak such blasphemy?!
Her Highness doth not covet food!
She... doth merely relish it!
Chime and I talk about when Crown looks most magnificent.

sessions.blurb: I possess a most extraordinary talent.

lines.text: I possess a most extraordinary talent.
Canst thou guess what it be?

choices.text: Your ability to assist Crown flawlessly?
Your quick reflexes?

lines.text: That can scarce be called a talent.
For a true aide, that much is but the very barest of basics.
Even thou wouldst do well to watch and learn, I say.
Hoho! Thou guessed it straight away.
Truly, thou hast an eye for such things.
'Tis not yet too late.
Shouldst thou wish to enter our kingdom as its advisor, thou shalt be welcomed at any hour!
Chime and I talk about her abilities.

sessions.blurb: *Groooowl*

lines.text: *Groooowl*
A-ahem!
Have ye aught to eat?

choices.text: Hand her some Splendamin.
Hand her a chocolate bar.

lines.text: Th-this is... Splendamin!
Hah, I shall not partake thereof!
Then, what about this?
I hand Chime a chocolate bar.
... I shall partake.
I-is it truly fine to bestow upon me something so precious?
... It hath been many years since I last tasted a chocolate bar.
My thanks, I shall enjoy it well.
Chime and I share a chocolate bar.

sessions.blurb: Hm? What art thou doing there?

lines.text: Hm? What art thou doing there?
Ah!
A cell phone, is it?
Hoho, how curious.
Chime's intense staring makes me feel uncomfortable.

choices.text: Hand Chime the phone.
Show Chime how to use the phone.

lines.text: Oh? Many thanks.
Hmm...
but how doth one handle this contraption again...?
Oooh.
Ooohhh!
So many new functions hath sprung up since I last laid eyes upon it.
Truly wondrous.
Pray, show me what other marvels it holds.
I show Chime the many functions of the cell phone.

sessions.blurb: Mark my words, Rapscallion...

lines.text: Mark my words, Rapscallion...
The day shall come when I tell thee of our grand mission.

choices.text: Okay, I'll wait until then.
Why not tell me now?

lines.text: Oho,
thy answer is brisk and most pleasing.
Keep thy spirit steadfast henceforth, and let it never falter.
N-nay, not now!
All things have their own time!
Thou must wait a little longer.
Chime and I have a serious conversation.

sessions.blurb: I have heard that thou dwellest in a place called the Outpost.

lines.text: I have heard that thou dwellest in a place called the Outpost.
How is it there? Is it livable, or doth it leave much to be desired?

choices.text: How about coming over and checking it out yourself?
It's not too bad.

lines.text: In person, thou sayest?
Thou wouldst invite me to thine dwelling?
Someday, I shall surely drop by with Her Highness.
Methinks I shall indeed set foot in your humble dwelling one day.
Rapscallion!
Speak not to me so half-heartedly!
Chime and I talk about the Outpost.

sessions.blurb: Well then, the remaining days be...

lines.text: Well then, the remaining days be...
Chime spins in place, muttering to herself.

choices.text: Strike up a conversation.
Wait for her to notice me.

lines.text: Silence, Rapscallion!
I was amidst most important calculations.
Now, on thy account, must I begin again from the very start!
A while later.
Phew... 'tis finished at last.
Oh? Thou hast been waiting for me?
My thanks for thy patience.
I was in the midst of some very important calculations, thou see'st.
I have a chat with Chime once she's done with her calculations.

sessions.blurb: Whene'er I traverse the surface,

lines.text: Whene'er I traverse the surface,
my meals are ever so paltry.
I long to return posthaste to the kingdom and partake of a proper feast.

choices.text: Can you actually get a proper meal there?
Want me to pass you some Splendamin?

lines.text: 'Tis of course.
We cook with that which we grow ourselves,
or with whatever we hunt and gather.
Forsooth, Her Highness taketh greatest delight in the dishes I prepare!
I thank thee,
but Splendamin is not to my taste.
Chime and I talk about the meals in the Crown Kingdom.

sessions.blurb: "He who does not work shall not eat," so the saying goes.

lines.text: "He who does not work shall not eat," so the saying goes.
What thinkest thou of this?

choices.text: So, does that mean Crown's going hungry?
Got it, I'll work hard.

lines.text: What? What nonsense speakest thou?
The mere fact that Her Highness is there
doth prove her hard work!
As expected, thou art quick-witted.
Thou pleasest me greatly.
Now, let us be off to work!
After our conversation ends, I help Chime with her work.

sessions.blurb: Pray tell, Rapscallion, between Her Highness and me,

lines.text: Pray tell, Rapscallion, between Her Highness and me,
who thinkest thou greater?

choices.text: Crown.
You.

lines.text: Aye, 'tis as thou sayest.
Her Highness is most magnificent,
so never forget that.
Rapscallion!
Speak not such falsehoods with bold confidence!
Chime begins to lavish praise on Crown.

sessions.blurb: Oh my... the sky hath turned all cloudy.

lines.text: Oh my... the sky hath turned all cloudy.
Methinks we are in for a downpour, I daresay.

choices.text: I'm sure it'll feel nice and refreshing.
Best to avoid it.

lines.text: Surely thou dost not mean to say...
thou enjoyest being drenched in the rain?
What a curious taste thou hast.
As for me, I shall seek shelter; I've no fondness for the rain.
Aye,
'tis most vexing to be soaked for no reason.
We must find shelter from this rain forthwith.
A little later, Chime and I watch the pouring rain together.

sessions.blurb: Rapscallion, art thou skilled in battle?

lines.text: Rapscallion, art thou skilled in battle?

choices.text: Yeah, I am.
No, not really.

lines.text: Oh? Is that truly so?
As I thought, thou art indeed capable!
Pray, tell me thy secret to fighting well.
I shall reward thee handsomely later.
No wonder...
I oft wondered why thou didst hide behind all in battle...
so 'tis because thou art poor at fighting, is it not?
Chime and I discuss ways to fight better.

sessions.blurb: Hm?

lines.text: Hm?
Why dost thou stare at me so?

choices.text: I just think you're cute.
I was just fascinated by the bell on your helmet.

lines.text: Thou darest tease me for being tiny?!
How audacious!
Oh, this?
'Tis useful in so many ways.
Wouldst thou try it thyself?
Chime and I while away the time with idle chatter.

sessions.blurb: The noble speech of Her Highness doth stir the hearts of all who hear it.

lines.text: The noble speech of Her Highness doth stir the hearts of all who hear it.
Dost thou not agree?

choices.text: Yeah... she's definitely dignified.
She messes up quite a few words, doesn't she?

lines.text: Indeed,
the dignity of Her Highness is the very force that upholds our kingdom.
And thou, Rapscallion, art at last nearing the rank of a true subject.
Wh-what blasphemy is this?!
Take back thy words this instant, or face my wrath!
I try imitating Crown's way of speaking with Chime.

sessions.blurb: Shall the day ever come when we reclaim the surface, I wonder?

lines.text: Shall the day ever come when we reclaim the surface, I wonder?
At times, I cannot help but feel a twinge of unease, alas.

choices.text: It'll come, I'm sure of it.
I can't help but feel uneasy too.

lines.text: ... Indeed!
They say the world bends to one's beliefs, dost it not?
Henceforth, I too shall hold fast to mine own faith!
What? Hmm...
I spoke naught but foolish words.
Let it be as if you heard naught.
Chime and I dream of reclaiming the surface.

sessions.blurb: I'm thinking of giving Her Highness a gift.

lines.text: I'm thinking of giving Her Highness a gift.
What thinkest thou might suit her best?

choices.text: Isn't that something you'd know best?
Hmm... wouldn't something simple be fine?

lines.text: Hah! 'Tis needless to say!
None knoweth Her Highness better than I, mark my words!
I shall present to her a gift most magnificent. Just thou wait and see!
Rapscallion!
Thy face screams of vexation!
Canst thou not think in earnest, just this once?
Chime and I discuss potential gifts for Crown.

sessions.blurb: Pray tell, what thinkest thou a kingdom to be?

lines.text: Pray tell, what thinkest thou a kingdom to be?

choices.text: A place where the subjects can live safely and in peace.
Well... a place where people gather?

lines.text: Indeed.
Her Highness and I do toil without rest for that very cause.
I must confess, it doth warm my heart to see thee recognize it.
How could a kingdom be such a trifling thing?!
Thou hast much yet to learn.
Chime and I have a deep discussion about what a kingdom is.

sessions.blurb: I have scouted the area thoroughly,

lines.text: I have scouted the area thoroughly,
yet there is little of value to be found.

choices.text: You've seen everything already? No way!
Already done? That was quick!

lines.text: Nonsense!
Dost thou accuse me of lying?
Know ye not
I possess the fleetest feet in all the kingdom?
Even Her Highness doth oft marvel at them.
Chime proceeds to boast at length about how fast she is.

sessions.blurb: We shall soon return to the Crown Kingdom.

lines.text: We shall soon return to the Crown Kingdom.
Wilt thou come with us, Rapscallion?

choices.text: Hmm, maybe I will.
Nah, not this time.

lines.text: What? T-truly?
I must inform Her Highness straightaway...!
W-wait! I'm just kidding.
Rapscallion! How darest thou make such a vile jest?!
Sorry... I'll be sure to go next time if I get the chance.
Hmph. Ever the same answer when I inquire.
Is it for the sake of thy comrades, then?
I nod my head.
Well, if that be so, it cannot be helped.
But do thou be sure to visit us someday.
Chime departs with a regretful expression.
